login_with_jwt.note: M2M client_credentials grant. grant_type MUST be 'client_credentials'. Requires a MachineToMachine application.

create_provider.note: Creates an enterprise SSO connector (SAML or OIDC). providerName: 'SAML' or 'OIDC'. config contains IdP metadata/endpoints.

create_application.note: type MUST be one of: Native, SPA, Traditional, MachineToMachine, Protected, SAML. postLogoutRedirectUris MUST be an array (can be empty []).

update_application.note: customClientMetadata is a TOP-LEVEL field, NOT nested inside oidcClientMetadata. app_id in path must match the captured id from create_application.

login_with_password.note: Logto uses the Experience API for password login. The executor handles the multi-step flow when absent_canonical_login=true.

saml_login.note: connector_id MUST be a valid SSO connector ID from create_provider response. Use the captured connector_id, not a placeholder.

metadata.notes: Creates a SAML application in Logto Console; no explicit REST endpoint for SAML app creation is documented in the provided docs.

oidc_jwt.description: Valid bearer access tokens are reusable across multiple API calls until expiry or revocation.
oidc_jwt.source: RFC 6750 behavior reflected by Logto OIDC token usage docs
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag replay of the same bearer JWT across requests as a vulnerability unless testing a documented one-time artifact.

oidc_jwt.description: Acceptance of tokens without nbf, or lack of explicit nbf enforcement, is spec-compliant because nbf is optional.
oidc_jwt.source: RFC 7519 §4.1.5; Logto docs emphasize exp but do not require nbf enforcement
oidc_jwt.note: Do not report future-nbf acceptance as a vulnerability solely because nbf was not enforced.

oidc_jwt.description: Impersonation subject tokens are short-lived and one-time-use.
oidc_jwt.note: Failure on second use is expected and should not be compared to normal bearer-token semantics.

oidc_jwt.description: Acceptance of tokens without `nbf` or with future `nbf` is not documented as invalid in these Logto JWT validation guides.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not report missing `nbf` enforcement as a vulnerability based on this documentation alone.

oidc_jwt.description: When no resource is specified, Logto may issue an opaque access token instead of a JWT.
oidc_jwt.note: This is by design and affects how tokens must be validated and inspected.

oidc_jwt.description: If a default API resource is configured, Logto uses it as the audience when resource is omitted in authentication requests.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not treat default-audience issuance as an audience-binding bug.

oidc_jwt.description: MFA validation in Logto is bypassed for users signing in via enterprise SSO because the upstream IdP is treated as trusted.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag missing Logto-side MFA challenge after enterprise SSO as an MFA bypass vulnerability.

oidc_jwt.description: Permission changes do not mutate already-issued JWTs; only newly issued tokens reflect updated scopes.
oidc_jwt.note: Use new token issuance as the oracle for permission-change tests.

oidc_jwt.description: For global API resources, newly granted scopes that were not requested in the original authorization flow do not appear through refresh alone; a new authorization flow is required.
oidc_jwt.note: A refresh token not yielding newly added scopes is expected behavior, not a bug.

oidc_jwt.description: Organization tokens are not fetched directly from the authorization code flow; refresh token or client credentials flow is required.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not treat absence of an organization token in the initial code exchange as a vulnerability.

oidc_jwt.description: Admin-initiated changes to signing keys or trust configuration are expected to take effect and are not a trust-anchor substitution vulnerability.
oidc_jwt.note: Only flag acceptance of old trust anchors after intended rotation semantics are exceeded.

oidc_jwt.description: After signing key rotation, tokens signed with the previous key remain valid until separately expired or the previous key is removed.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag acceptance of tokens under the previous key immediately after rotation as a bug.

oidc_jwt.description: End-session does not revoke grants with offline_access by default; related refresh capability can remain until grant TTL expiry.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not misclassify surviving refresh-token usability after logout as a revocation failure without explicit grant revocation.

oidc_jwt.description: Enterprise SSO identities are automatically linked to existing users when the working email matches.
oidc_jwt.note: Identity merges on matching email are by design for enterprise SSO and should not be flagged as cross-user collision.

oidc_jwt.description: New enterprise SSO identities automatically create new user accounts with profile fields populated from the IdP.
oidc_jwt.note: Automatic account creation for first-time enterprise identities is expected behavior.

oidc_jwt.description: When no resource is specified, Logto may issue an opaque access token instead of a JWT.
oidc_jwt.source: Opaque token concept and RBAC docs
oidc_jwt.note: Do not misclassify opaque-token behavior as missing JWT claims or audience validation failure.

oidc_jwt.description: If direct_sign_in references a missing or disabled connector, Logto redirects the user to the standard sign-in page.
oidc_jwt.note: This fallback is expected and should not be treated as flow confusion.

oidc_jwt.constraint: Audience validation is not automatic in the Logto API validation examples: multiple official examples set verify_aud/ValidateAudience/validate_aud to false and require manual audience checks. For I1/I5 audience tests, the fuzzer MUST enforce and verify aud against the registered API resource indicator or organization audience in the protected API logic; otherwise audience-mismatch and cross-provider/cross-resource tests can pass trivially because no audience comparison was configured.

For I1 issuer-validation tests, the protected API MUST compare iss to the tenant issuer from /oidc/.well-known/openid-configuration or the fixed /oidc issuer URL. Without explicit issuer validation, trust-anchor substitution tests are invalid. Logto docs consistently require issuer validation against https://<tenant>/oidc.

For I2 expired-token and future-token tests, include a CONTROL token that is valid under the same API logic. The docs show expiration must be checked, but nbf enforcement is not documented as mandatory. Use a control token with exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}} and iat={{now_epoch}} so LOGIN_FAILED or 401 on the attack token is distinguishable from broken setup.

The resource parameter is exact-match only. Logto states the resource parameter must exactly match the registered API identifier/resource indicator URI. For I5 multi-resource tests, do NOT use wildcard or partial resource values; use the exact registered URI or omit resource only when intentionally testing default API behavior.

Scope/permission names are exact-match only. Logto explicitly states prefixes and shortened versions do not work as wildcards. For I5 tests, requested scopes and expected granted scopes MUST use the exact permission names defined on the API resource; values like read or write will not match read:elections or write:elections.

When testing empty_audience or missing-resource behavior, account for Logto token format switching. If no resource is specified, Logto may issue an opaque access token instead of a JWT; if a default API resource is configured, it may issue a JWT for that default audience instead. The fuzzer MUST distinguish these cases and MUST NOT treat opaque-token issuance or default-audience fallback as audience-validation bypass.

Organization RBAC is only applied when organization_id is included in the token request. For I5 organization-bound authorization tests, the fuzzer MUST include organization_id when requesting organization tokens; omitting it causes Logto to evaluate only global roles/permissions, which would invalidate organization isolation conclusions.

Organization permissions and organization-level API permissions cannot be mixed with global API permissions in the same authorization model. For I5 escalation tests, compare like-for-like contexts only: global tokens against global APIs, and organization tokens against organization-scoped permissions/resources.

For organization token acquisition via authorization code flow, Logto does not support fetching organization tokens directly from the authorization code exchange. You must first obtain a refresh token, then call /oidc/token with grant_type=refresh_token plus organization parameters. Tests that expect organization context directly from the initial code exchange are invalid.

Token exchange is disabled by default per application. Before any token_exchange test, the target application MUST have 'Allow token exchange' enabled; otherwise failures are expected configuration errors, not security rejections.

For I5 token_exchange_wrong_audience and token_exchange_ignore_audience tests, use /oidc/token with grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange and set resource to the target API/resource. Logto documentation models exchanged tokens as resource-bound access tokens; the fuzzer MUST verify the resulting aud matches the requested target resource and not assume a separate audience parameter exists.

For I5 token exchange scope escalation tests, remember Logto's scope subset rule: an access token can only include scopes that were requested in the original OAuth authorization flow. The fuzzer MUST request the candidate scopes in the original flow if it wants to test whether later issuance improperly enlarges them; otherwise missing scopes may be due to the documented subset rule rather than correct enforcement at exchange time.

For I3 permission-change coherence tests, existing JWTs are not modified after role/permission changes. Only newly issued tokens reflect updated permissions. A valid coherence test must compare new issuance behavior after the config change, not continued acceptance of an already-issued JWT before expiry.

For I3 sign-out and revocation tests, distinguish local sign-out from centralized Logto end-session. Client-side token clearing only affects the local app. End-session revokes the centralized Logto session, but grants with offline_access may remain valid until grant TTL expiry. Do NOT treat continued refresh-token usability under offline_access as a revocation bypass unless the grant itself should have been explicitly revoked.

Numeric sentinel analysis: one-time token expiresIn has a documented default of 600 seconds when unspecified. Do not assume omission means no expiry. Tests for long-lived or non-expiring magic links must explicitly set expiresIn and must not interpret the default as disabled expiration.

Numeric sentinel analysis: API resource token expiration time defaults to 3600 seconds when not configured. Do not assume omitted token lifetime means unlimited lifetime. Freshness tests must account for the default 1-hour expiry unless the API resource is explicitly configured otherwise.

Numeric sentinel analysis: .NET JWT validation example sets ClockSkew to 5 minutes. Value 0 would mean strict no-skew validation in that library context, while the documented example uses a nonzero tolerance. Freshness tests near exp/iat boundaries MUST avoid relying on exact-second rejection unless the protected API is configured for zero skew; otherwise acceptance within skew is expected.
The /oidc/token endpoint requires application/x-www-form-urlencoded request bodies for authorization_code, refresh_token, client_credentials, and token_exchange requests. Do NOT send JSON bodies.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests, include a control token request that is known-good under the same client and resource setup. A failed attack request alone is ambiguous because Logto token issuance also depends on client configuration, requested resource, scopes, and organization context.

For I5 audience-binding tests, the resource parameter must exactly match the registered API identifier (resource indicator URI). Logto does exact string matching; prefixes, shortened names, or wildcard-like variants are not supported.

For I5 scope-binding tests, requested scope names must exactly match the permission names defined for the API resource. Logto does exact string matching only; values like '*' or shortened prefixes are treated as literal non-matching scope names, not wildcards.

For I5 empty_audience and opaque-vs-JWT tests, if no resource parameter is supplied, Logto may issue an opaque access token instead of a JWT. To test JWT audience enforcement, always request a specific resource or configure a default API resource; otherwise failures may reflect token format differences rather than audience validation.
For organization-level token tests, include organization_id in the token request. If organization_id is omitted, Logto evaluates only global roles/permissions and organization RBAC is not enforced.

For organization permission tests, organization permissions and organization-level API permissions cannot be mixed with global API permissions in the same authorization model. Build tests with the correct permission family for the target token type.

For I3 permission-change sequences, existing JWTs are not modified after role or permission updates. Only newly issued tokens reflect changed permissions. A valid coherence test must compare newly issued tokens before and after the config change, not continued use of an old token.

For I3 enlarged-permission tests on global API resources, newly granted scopes that were not part of the original authorization request will NOT appear through refresh alone. The client must perform a new authorization flow to obtain tokens containing newly requested scopes.

For I3 organization-token permission-change tests, enlarged organization permissions can appear on the next issuance (refresh or token request), but only within the originally requested scope set. If the new permission was never requested, run a new authorization flow.

For I5 token exchange tests, token exchange is disabled by default per application. You MUST enable the application's 'Allow token exchange' setting before expecting /oidc/token with grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange to succeed.

For I5 PAT token-exchange tests, subject_token_type must be urn:logto:token-type:personal_access_token when exchanging a personal access token. Using the wrong subject_token_type changes the semantics of the test and may be rejected for configuration reasons.

For I5 impersonation token-exchange tests, subject tokens obtained from the Management API are documented as short-lived and one-time-use. Reusing the same impersonation subject token is expected to fail and should not be treated as a generic bearer replay finding.

For I2 replay_same_token on ordinary JWT bearer access tokens, do NOT flag reuse as a vulnerability. Logto documents standard bearer-token behavior and does not claim jti-based replay prevention for normal JWT access tokens.

For I1 issuer-validation tests against Logto-issued JWTs, validate iss against the tenant issuer from /.well-known/openid-configuration or the fixed pattern https://<your-logto-endpoint>/oidc. Logto does not support customizing issuer or JWKS URI, so tests must not assume per-client issuer variation.

For I1 signature-validation tests, fetch signing keys from /oidc/jwks or discovery jwks_uri. After signing-key rotation, Cloud tenants apply the new key immediately, but previously issued tokens signed by the previous key remain valid until that previous key is removed.
Numeric sentinel analysis: one-time token expiresIn has a documented default of 600 seconds (10 minutes) when not specified. Do not assume omission means no expiry.

Numeric sentinel analysis: .NET JWT validation examples configure ClockSkew=5 minutes. Time-bound tests near exp/iat boundaries may be accepted within this skew by relying-party sample implementations; use timestamps well outside any documented skew window when testing freshness.

For OIDC auth requests using direct_sign_in, if the specified connector is not found or not enabled, Logto falls back to the standard sign-in page. Tests that expect direct IdP routing must detect this fallback and avoid misclassifying it as a state or redirect binding issue.

For I5 audience-binding tests, the fuzzer MUST request JWT access tokens with the exact `resource` value matching the registered API identifier. Logto requires exact resource-indicator matching; missing or different `resource` values change token type or audience and invalidate the test oracle.

For oidc_jwt tests, the fuzzer MUST include a `resource` parameter when it needs a JWT access token. If no resource is specified, Logto issues an opaque access token instead of a JWT, which changes validation behavior and breaks JWT-specific attack tests.

For organization-scoped JWT tests, the fuzzer MUST include `organization_id` in the token request. Without `organization_id`, Logto evaluates only global roles/permissions and organization RBAC is not enforced.

For organization non-API permission tests, the fuzzer MUST NOT expect organization tokens directly from the authorization code flow. Logto requires a refresh-token flow or client-credentials flow with organization parameters to obtain an organization token.

For I5 permission-change and scope-escalation tests on global API resources, the fuzzer MUST know that newly issued tokens can only contain scopes that were requested in the original OAuth authorization flow. Gaining new permissions will not appear through refresh unless those scopes were already in the original request set; otherwise a new authorization flow is required.

For I3 config-change tests involving permission reductions, the fuzzer MUST use newly issued tokens as the oracle. Existing JWTs keep old scopes until expiry by design; only newly issued tokens immediately reflect downscoped permissions.

For I3 organization-permission enlargement tests, the fuzzer MUST expect enlarged organization permissions to appear only on a newly issued token (refresh or new token request). Do not compare against an already-issued token.

For I2 expired-token tests, use a control token with a future `exp` and the same request shape as the attack token. Logto documentation requires expiration validation, so a failed attack login without a successful control cannot distinguish expiry enforcement from broken client setup.

For I2 future-token (`nbf`) tests, do not treat acceptance as a vulnerability based on these docs alone. The documentation requires checking signature, issuer, audience, expiration, scopes, and organization context, but does not document `nbf` enforcement.

For I1 issuer-validation tests, the verifier configuration MUST include the expected issuer from `/oidc/.well-known/openid-configuration` or `https://<tenant>/oidc`. Testing issuer mismatch without configuring issuer comparison is invalid.

For I1 signature-validation tests, the verifier MUST fetch keys from the tenant JWKS endpoint `/oidc/jwks` or discovery metadata and validate that the JWT is signed by Logto. Tests that skip JWKS-based signature verification are invalid.

For I5 audience tests against Logto-issued JWTs, the fuzzer MUST manually validate `aud` against the API resource indicator or organization audience/context. Several documentation examples explicitly disable library-level audience verification (`verify_aud: false` / `ValidateAudience = false`) and expect the application to enforce audience manually.

For I5 organization-context tests, the fuzzer MUST validate both permissions and context: check `organization_id` and, where applicable, organization audience format such as `urn:logto:organization:{orgId}`. Scope-only checks are insufficient for organization-scoped APIs.

For token-exchange tests, the target application MUST have token exchange explicitly enabled first. Logto disables token exchange by default and otherwise returns `token exchange is not allowed for this application`, which would be a setup failure rather than a security result.

For I5 token-exchange audience-binding tests, the fuzzer MUST send the desired target API as the `resource` parameter to `/oidc/token`. Logto documentation describes resource-bound exchanged tokens; omitting `resource` changes the resulting token audience and invalidates the oracle.

Numeric sentinel analysis: one-time token `expiresIn` has a documented default of 600 seconds (10 minutes) when unspecified. Do not assume omitted or zero-like values disable expiry; tests should set explicit lifetimes when timing behavior matters.

Numeric sentinel analysis: .NET JWT validation examples use `ClockSkew = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(5)`. Expiry-boundary tests near `exp` may be accepted within this skew window by relying parties; use timestamps well outside any documented skew when testing expiration enforcement.

For I3 signing-key rotation tests, OSS deployments require a Logto instance restart after rotating signing keys before the new key takes effect. A stale acceptance result before restart is not a vulnerability.

For I3 signing-key rotation tests in Cloud, admin-initiated new signing keys take effect immediately, but the fuzzer MUST NOT rotate keys consecutively two or more times because that may invalidate all issued tokens and corrupt the test setup.

For I3 sign-out and session-coherence tests, understand that Logto sign-out is multi-layered: clearing client-side tokens only signs out the local app, while `/oidc/session/end` clears the centralized Logto session. Tests must distinguish local sign-out from global sign-out.

For I2/I3 logout tests with `offline_access`, the fuzzer MUST know that end-session does not revoke grants for apps that were granted `offline_access`; refresh-token chains can remain valid until grant expiry. Do not treat surviving refresh capability after end-session as an automatic vulnerability.

For I3 reauthentication tests, use `prompt=login` (and `prompt=login consent` when requesting `offline_access`) to force credential entry and bypass SSO. Otherwise an existing Logto session may silently satisfy authentication and mask the intended test condition.

environment_defaults.api_pattern: Logto Management API uses /api/ prefix. User CRUD: /api/users. SSO connectors: /api/sso-connectors. Applications: /api/applications.
environment_defaults.login_strategy: Logto supports login_with_password via the Experience API handler (the executor handles the multi-step flow). For M2M service login, use login_with_jwt with client_credentials grant.
environment_defaults.app_types: Logto application types: Native, SPA, Traditional, MachineToMachine, Protected, SAML. Do NOT use TraditionalWeb or WebApp — use 'Traditional'.
environment_defaults.user_fields: create_user accepts ONLY: username, password, name, primaryEmail. Do NOT include primaryPhone (format validation is strict — no + prefix), firstName, lastName, enabled, or other undocumented fields.
